previous_description: Statement of need that must be realized by a system, component, or solution, and that can be associated with stakeholders, goals, or constraints.
definition: A statement of need that a system, component, or solution must realize, phrased as a specific, verifiable behavior or property (typically a 'shall/must' statement with acceptance criteria) and traceable to the stakeholders, drivers, or goals that motivate it.

distinguish_from.when: the statement expresses a high-level desired direction or end state that cannot be directly verified against a specific system, rather than a concrete need the system must meet
the statement limits the design or implementation options (e.g. a mandated technology, budget, deadline, or regulation) rather than stating something the system must do or exhibit
the statement is a general normative rule that applies to all systems in a context and guides decisions, rather than a need assigned to a particular system or solution
the statement describes a measurable end result the organization intends or has achieved, rather than a property the system must have to contribute to it

code_evidence: A requirements document, PRD, or SRS entry with a stable identifier (e.g. REQ-042, FR-7, NFR-3) and 'shall'/'must' wording
A user story or issue tracker ticket labeled as a requirement, with acceptance criteria that tests or reviewers check against
Test annotations, docstrings, or traceability matrices that reference a requirement ID (e.g. @Requirement("REQ-042"), '# Verifies NFR-3') linking code or tests back to the stated need

attribute_descriptions.name: documentation
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text statement of the requirement, including its full wording, rationale, source, and acceptance or verification criteria; set it whenever the name alone does not make the need verifiable.

notes: ArchiMate treats Constraint as a specialization of Requirement; the boundary needs explicit rules. requirementType 'regulatory' overlaps constraintType 'regulatory', and 'non-functional' overlaps 'quality'. Consider merging these values. 'requirement aggregates goal' inverts the normal direction. Incoming links mix 'satisfies', 'realizes', and 'fulfills' inconsistently. Consider adding a verification/acceptanceCriteria attribute.
